audit_findings.title: The $795 million joint-venture bridge may double count earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $795 million bridge addition; $60 million filed carrying value; $735 million difference equals $19.33 per diluted share; affiliate earnings were $10 million, $11 million and $15 million in 2023-2025
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the joint-venture interest separately, while any affiliate earnings retained in OE are also capitalized through operating PV and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s share of equity in income or losses is included in Equity in affiliates’ earnings, net of tax in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that affiliate earnings enter GAAP income, but it does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation removed them. Thus double counting is unresolved rather than proven. Independently, the $795 million bridge value lacks supplied support and exceeds carrying value by $735 million. Carrying value need not equal fair value, but removing only that unsupported excess would reduce base value by $19.33 per share and would change the buy-below conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to removal of the $10 million, $11 million and $15 million affiliate earnings, obtain the valuation supporting $795 million, and rerun all scenarios using PHINIA's realizable 52.5% proceeds after taxes, transaction costs and applicable discounts.

audit_findings.title: An unreserved legacy emissions claim may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: An unaccrued fine, recall, remediation cost or settlement would reduce the equity bridge or future OE when paid; recurring legal costs alone do not capture the claim principal.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the Separation and Distribution Agreement we entered into with the Former Parent in connection with the Spin-Off, we are generally allocated responsibility for any consequences arising out of the German investigation and any similar investigations.
audit_findings.explanation: The investigation and PHINIA's contractual responsibility are demonstrated, but neither a probable loss nor a reasonably possible loss range is supplied. This is therefore a present unresolved contingent claim, not a demonstrated valuation error. Its potential effect could be material, but the record cannot establish its amount or probability.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current investigation status, counsel's probability and loss range, product population and recall exposure, insurance and indemnity recoveries, then rerun the bridge with probability-weighted and adverse-case payments separate from recurring OE.

audit_findings.title: The Spin-Off tax indemnity is an unquantified senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: If triggered, the indemnity would create a cash claim ahead of common equity and reduce the bridge or forecast OE in the payment period.
audit_findings.evidence: If, as a result of any of our representations being untrue or our covenants being breached, the Spin-Off were determined not to qualify for its intended tax-free treatment, we could be required by the Tax Matters Agreement and any amendments or restatements thereto to indemnify the Former Parent for the resulting taxes and related expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The indemnity obligation exists contractually, but the record supplies no covenant breach, IRS challenge, asserted claim or loss estimate. It is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated liability. Because the filing says resulting taxes and expenses could be material, the possibility cannot be dismissed, but materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Review the amended Tax Matters Agreement, covenant compliance, survival and limitation provisions, tax opinions, IRS examination status and any notices from the former parent; rerun only if evidence supports a probability-weighted or scenario loss.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded pension deficit is not visibly captured
audit_findings.magnitude: $142 million filed deficit at December 31, 2025, equal to $3.73 per diluted share and 3.6% of base equity value; June 30, 2026 retirement-related liabilities were $134 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any deficit not already represented by OE cash contributions is a claim ahead of equity and belongs in the bridge; required contributions above normalized pension expense would also reduce forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The funded status of all pension plans was a net unfunded position of $142 million and $113 million at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The deficit is demonstrated and no pension adjustment appears in the bridge, but the supplied record does not show whether OE already deducts actual contributions or otherwise captures the funding burden. A full $142 million deduction would reduce base value to about $99.90 per share and buy-below to about $69.93, still slightly above the $69.04 price but materially narrowing the decision margin. The incremental adjustment therefore remains uncertain and must avoid double counting.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense and actual contributions within every OE year, obtain current plan-by-plan funded status and required contribution schedules, then rerun with the tax-adjusted incremental deficit or excess contributions not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not all be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $370 million added to the bridge, or $9.73 per diluted share; $352 million was held outside the United States; approximately $150 million was committed for the proposed stoba acquisition
audit_findings.mechanism: Only distributable excess cash belongs in the bridge; operating cash, restricted or costly-to-repatriate balances, and committed acquisition funding must be excluded unless the corresponding acquired-business value is also included.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 the Company had cash and cash equivalent balance of $359 million, of which $330 million was held by our subsidiaries outside of the United States.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation adds all $370 million, while the filing establishes that 95% was held outside the United States and identifies a proposed $150 million cash-funded acquisition. Foreign location does not itself make cash unavailable, but the distributable amount is not established. If more than roughly $190 million is unavailable or committed without corresponding acquired value, the base buy-below conclusion would reverse.
audit_findings.action: Map June 2026 cash by entity and jurisdiction, quantify legal restrictions, withholding and repatriation taxes, minimum operating cash and committed uses, reconcile the stoba purchase price with any acquired operating value, and rerun the bridge using only net distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The OE anchor capitalizes potentially conditional government support
audit_findings.magnitude: $29 million pre-tax credits in 2025, comprising $24 million in SG&A and $5 million in cost of sales; comparable credits were $30 million in 2024 and $22 million in 2023; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Grant credits increase the OE anchor and are consequently grown and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Company recorded $ 24 million, $ 28 million and $ 21 million of government grant-related credits in Selling, general and administrative expenses, respectively, and $ 5 million, $ 2 million and $ 1 million in Cost of sales, respectively, in the Company’s Consolidated Statement of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The credits are demonstrated and recurring across three reported years, so their inclusion is not automatically erroneous. However, the supplied record does not establish program duration, conditions, incremental qualifying costs or availability during the terminal period. The 2025 amount is 14.7% of the $197.6 million anchor before adjusting for its specific tax effect, making unsupported perpetual capitalization reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify each grant, remaining term, renewal basis, clawback conditions and associated incremental costs; determine the grant-specific after-tax recurring benefit and rerun the explicit and terminal periods with benefits ending when contractual support ends.
